summary: Agents can now debug, not just read and run: they set breakpoints, start a test under the debugger and look at the stack and variables, all in Arro's own Debug window. Errors go to an agent from where you see them, with Fix with AI. The AI Sessions window got simpler, shows who is connected over MCP, and lets you select and copy text. The SQL console can format, expand templates and run .sql files.

items.html: The debugger over MCP. Agents can set and remove breakpoints (with conditions and log messages), start a test or a run configuration under the debugger (with your permission), wait for a stop, read the stack and the variables, evaluate an expression and step. Everything shows in the Debug window and the editor, and you can continue or stop the session yourself.

items.html: Spell checking. Typos in comments, Javadoc, string literals, declaration names, Markdown, .properties, YAML and XML comments get a green wavy underline. camelCase and snake_case words are split, and short words, URLs, paths and hex are skipped. Alt+Enter offers up to five replacements: a typo in a declaration is fixed through Rename, so its usages change too. You can also save the word to the project or application dictionary, or turn the check off. Words come from the system spell checker on Windows and macOS and from hunspell or /usr/share/dict/words on Linux. Settings → Editor → Spelling edits your dictionary, and the Typo inspection has its own level.
